thread:
Sam G: Heads up — BlueOak is seeing a sudden flood of 429s right now on the /v1/generate chat route. Started ~09:22 UTC, pretty spiky, roughly aligned to minute boundaries. They report 50-80 reqs/s dropping to lots of 429s at the top of the minute. Can we triage?
Olivia H: Thanks — do we have a sample request_id or tenant_id from the logs? minute-boundary spikes usually point to token refill/cron alignment or client-side retries aligning.
Sam G: tenant=blueoak-tenant, request_id=rcq-9f7a3, region=us-west-2. Route: POST /v1/chat/generate model=redwood-1-large stream=false. Customer says clients multiplex across HTTP/2 and also have a small batcher that fires every minute.
Mia S: Two quick checks: 1) confirm x-rate-limit headers in responses (x-ratelimit-limit, x-ratelimit-remaining, x-ratelimit-reset) — sometimes proxies strip them. 2) check if their requests are mostly small (1-2 tokens) or long — TPM vs RPM matters.
Sam G: I pulled the headers from a few 429 responses: `x-ratelimit-limit: 6000`, `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `x-ratelimit-reset: 168000` (example). Also saw `x-tenant-rpm: 3600` in our logs.
Nate P: Sounds like they're hitting a per-tenant RPM cap (3600/min ~60 reqs/s). If they burst above that for a short period due to minute folding they’ll see 429s until reset. Are the spikes sustained or short pulses at the minute mark?
Sam G: Short pulses concentrated at t:00 - t:01 (top of each minute) — lasts ~3-7s, then clears.
Olivia H: Classic minute folding. Likely causes: cron-aligned batcher + client retry loops without jitter + HTTP/2 stream reuse causing many concurrent requests to be dispatched when a token refill happens. Customer-side mitigations: add jitter to batch times, smooth batcher into smaller slices, add client-side concurrency limits and exponential backoff with full jitter.
Support L2: We should collect: 1) a 5-minute log window (request_id, timestamp, route, response_code, x-* headers), 2) a traffic sample showing per-second rate from the edge (per-tenant), and 3) their client retry/backoff config. Can we ask BlueOak for a short tcpdump or client logs?
Sam G: I asked BlueOak for client logs and their batch schedule (they run a minute-based sync at :00 every minute). They confirmed no jitter.
Mia S: Platform-side: we can enable transient burst smoothing for them if they need a short-term fix while they patch clients. Also check if they are on a shared RPM pool vs dedicated. If shared, we may need a temporary rate cap override or emergency quota bump.
Ratecap Bot: [alert] tenant=blueoak-tenant exceeded RPM quota at 1759876568 (3608 RPM)
Nate P: To reproduce quickly, run a replay with their headers and timing. Example curl for a 8 req/s steady, then a 120 req burst for 6s: ```bash
# steady
for i in {1..48}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Tenant: blueoak-tenant" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/generate &
  sleep 0.020
done
# burst
for i in {1..120}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Tenant: blueoak-tenant" -d '{"input":"burst"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/generate &
done
wait
```
Olivia H: Good repro. When you run that, capture our edge-per-second metric and x-* headers. If you see `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0` immediately after the burst, it's RPM cap.
Sam G: Ran the repro in staging with their tenant id and saw the same pattern: immediate 429s during the 6s burst, then returns to 200 afterwards. Collected edge-per-second graph and attached to ticket (link pasted to customer).
Support L2: Suggested immediate actions for BlueOak: 1) Add 250-500ms random jitter to their batch schedule, 2) cap concurrent HTTP/2 streams to 8 per client, 3) implement exponential backoff with full jitter for 429s, and 4) consider spreading their batch across 10s windows instead of one spike.
Mia S: Suggested platform-side temporary remedies: 1) grant a +20% burst override (non-persistent) for 24h, 2) enable smoothing on shared pool for tenant=blueoak-tenant, 3) create an alert for per-tenant per-second > 80 for more than 5s. Do we have an owner for temporary quota change?
Sam G: I can file the quota bump request with ops; tagging @Nate P to approve. Also sent BlueOak a short playbook for client changes.
Nate P: Approved transient +20% bump for 6 hours (ops ticket #OP-3781). Also set alert as requested. Please do not make permanent quota changes until product approves.
Support L2: I'll follow up with the customer in 30m to confirm changes reduced 429s. If they still see issues we'll propose a proper Dedicated plan or a scheduled quota increase.
Olivia H: For postmortem notes: log snippet collection, replay commands used, timeline, and client config. Add recommended SDK changes to our docs for "minute-fold smoothing".
Sam G: Thanks team — will update ticket and notify BlueOak. :thumbsup:
BlueOak (via Sam G): "Implemented jitter and reduced stream concurrency — immediate improvement. 429s dropped to near zero in last 10 mins."
Support L2: Marking thread for follow-up tomorrow to ensure changes are stable.
